1→HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 20210 of 2012
Court No. - 1 
HON'BLE AJIT KUMAR, J.
HON'BLE SWARUPAMA CHATURVEDI, J.
1. Heard Sri Bidhan Chandra Rai, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri 
Dinesh Rai, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri Ram Chandra, 
learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned counsel 
appearing for respondent concerned and learned Standing Counsel appearing 
10→for State respondent.
2. Petitioner before this Court, who is electricity consumer of respondents 
corporation having industrial connection, is aggrieved by the order passed by 
the appellate authority dated 09.04.2012 under Section 127 of the Electricity 
Act, 2003 and has thus questioned the same. 
3. Sri Bidhan Chandra Rai, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the 
petitioner while assailing the order of final assessment passed under the U.P. 
Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and the order passed by the appellate 
authority has raised two fold arguments which are as follows:-
(i) The authority after having a surprise checking of the electricity meter of 
20→the petitioner since failed to find out any tempering with the main meter 
except the loose seal of the godrej lock put on the outer box of the meter, 
manifestly erring in arriving at a conclusion that there was an unauthorized 
use of the electricity by the petitioner calling for an action under the U.P. 
Electricity Act, 2003 read with relevant provisions of the Electricity Supply 
Code, 2005 for the purpose of penal charges on the basis of provisional and 
final assessment. 
Versus
Counsel for Petitioner(s)
:
30→B.C. Rai, Dinesh Rai, Stuti Rai
Counsel for Respondent(s)
:
Pranjal Mehrotra, C.S.C., N.Misra, 
Pankaj Kumar Shukla
M/S Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd.
.....Petitioner(s)
State of U.P. and Others
.....Respondent(s)

40→(ii) Respondents have not accorded due consideration to the points raised 
before the assessing authority and further the appellate authority fell in 
serious error of law in failing to consider the ground raised in the appeal.
4. Both the impugned orders of final assessment and the appellate authority 
are, therefore, are to be rendered unsustainable and deserve to be quashed. 
5. From the perusal of pleadings, it clearly transpires that there was no 
dispute between the parties that the petitioner had a valid meter for industrial 
connection of electricity and that on 22.06.2007 a surprise check took place 
in which the outer box of the electricity meter of the petitioner was found to 
be with broken seal. It is also not disputed that in the conclusion drawn by 
50→the inspecting team, it was not a case of theft of electricity as no direct theft 
of electricity had been detected in metering system of M/s Kamakhya Steels 
Pvt. Ltd. and the assessment was made considering it to be a case of 
possibility of theft. 
6. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that with the installation of 
meter, the same was sealed again by removing the old seal in presence of the 
petitioner and under the signature of the petitioner, a seal certificate was 
issued. A surprise check of the meter took place on 22.06.2007 in the current 
transformer and potential transformer (CT and PT). They were found to be 
physically 'OK' with no abnormality and only MRI cord with which the 
60→meter reading instrument is attached for the purpose of meter reading was 
found to be defective. The report vide its clause 8 reported the meter cubicle 
and double pole meter were found to be as per norms and only CT/PT 
chamber was found to be not properly sealed. On the basis of this inspection, 
a checking report was submitted on 26.06.2007, in which it is submitted on 
behalf of the petitioner, when it has come that MRI and reading was carried 
out on 21.06.2007 and there was no report of any abnormality, how could 
there be any electricity dues liable for alleged possibility of theft prior to that 
date. 
7. Sri Rai has further taken the Court to the godrej lock that was put on the 
70→meter room, found to be not properly sealed and after removing the M-Seal, 
it was preserved in a box. It is also submitted that after analyzing the entire 
meter, the authority has presented in the checking report that a clear case of 
theft was ruled out and hence according to Sri Rai, on a mere apprehension 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
2

of possibility of theft, no conclusion can be drawn that the theft was 
committed. Sri Rai led an argument that theft is a question of fact and unless 
and until, it is proved beyond doubt, a mere doubt or apprehension cannot 
80→form a proved/stablished case of theft to lead the authority competent in the 
matter to hold that the petitioner was liable to pay charges for unauthorized 
use of electricity. 
8. Sri Rai has further argued that the notice dated 18.07.2007 mentioned 
electricity loss of 9.17% to 19.75% for unauthorized use by the petitioner, is 
also not believable for the reason that the petitioner was not the only 
consumer but there were two others namely, M/s Jain Steel and 33/11 KV 
S/S Avas Vikas Feeder having electricity supply from 132 KV feeder at 
Bijnor and Avas Vikas at 33/11 KV feeder to have a sub-station line, 
therefore, consumption or loss of line was not mainly attributable to the 
90→petitioner. Sri Rai submits that he had raised all these points in his objection 
filed on 30.07.2007 but they all went unnoticed by the Executive Engineer 
who passed the order of final assessment. Sri Rai also submits that the order 
of final assessment is absolutely sans consideration of the objections raised 
by the petitioner and hence it is liable to be rendered as unsustainable. 
9. Sri Rai further submits that since the point raised were not accorded due 
consideration by the final assessing authority, the petitioner preferred the 
appeal raising all those points as facts pleaded in the appeal and also the 
grounds raised but none of the grounds have been considered and the appeal 
has also been dismissed in a summary manner. It is argued lastly by learned 
100→Senior Advocate that the petitioner has already made a deposit which is an 
extra deposit being in excess to what the petitioner was liable to pay and 
hence petitioner is entitled to refund. 
10. Sri Ram Chandra, learned Advocate holding brief of Sri Pranjal 
Mehrotra, learned counsel appearing for respondent concerned has justified 
the orders, both final assessment as well as the order of the appellate 
authority for the reasons assigned therein and has placed paragraph nos. 6, 
10 and 17 thereof. According to him, writ petition is devoid of merit and 
deserves to be dismissed. 
11. Having heard the learned counsel for respective parties and having 
110→perused the record, we find it to be an admitted fact of position between the 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
3

parties that MRI of the meter in question was conducted on 21.06.2021 but 
no such report was submitted about any error indicating by-pass of the meter 
cable for the consumption of electricity or breaking of its seal. However, 
petitioner was not supplied with the MRI report to contest the same if 
anything adverse was therein. This plea has been taken in para no. 9 of the 
writ petition. In reply thereof, only this much has been stated that the 
120→officers of the electricity department had raided the premises on 22.06.2007 
and found unauthorized use of electricity and then they prepared the 
checking report with certain details like holo seals on meter box, CT 
chamber, TP and double box bore no signature of any officer/official, CT/PT 
seal of the meter chamber was found to be tempered and m-seal was used for 
joining the bottom and top part of the seal, wax layer was found pasted on 
the seal above the painted metal surface to facilitate easy removal of M-Seal 
without damaging it for opening the door lock of CT/PT chamber, MRI cord 
was found defective, SE(D) Bijnor and E.E. ETD Bijnor were requested to 
seal the meter cubicle and double pole meter as per norms and consumer 
130→refused to sign the inspection memo. 
12. If the above averments are taken to be answer to paragraph no. 9, then in 
our considered view, it is highly misplaced an answer. Neither in the writ 
petition, nor in the objection filed by the petitioner, petitioner has doubted 
the recitals contained in in the report, instead what the petitioner submitted 
that if the MRI reading was conducted on 21.06.2007, a day before surprise 
checking was done, the said report ought to have been also supplied to the 
petitioner. Further what the petitioner contended throughout in objection and 
in appeal and even before this Court that while outer box of the meter was 
found to be with tempered seal or that godrej lock of the meter room was 
140→also not found properly sealed. There was no report that the original meter 
seal was broken or any tempering was done that the meter so as to draw a 
conclusion that some by-pass was created to consume the electricity reading 
to avoid meter reading, which would have amounted to theft. The Court 
cannot ignore conclusion part of the summary report of the checking which 
clearly states that "Although no direct theft of electricity has been detected in 
metering system of M/s Kamakhya Steel Pvt. Ltd. But following facts lead to 
conclude the possibility of theft."
13. Now what fact led the authority to conclude possibility of theft was as 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
150→4

follows:-
(i) Tempered seals of CT/PT chamber of main meter.
(ii) Considerable difference (varying from 9.17% to 19.75%) in energy sent 
from 132KV sub-station Bijnor and the total sum of receipt of energies of all 
the three consumers connected on the 33KV feeder namely,  M/s Kamakhya 
Steels Pvt. Ltd., M/s Jain Steel and 33/11 KV S/S Avas Vikas Feeder.
14. A clear cut objection was raised that the meter seal having not been 
found broken and no discrepancies whatsoever having been detected in the 
160→meter, firstly, it could not be said that there was a theft, and secondly, the 
cause of assumed line loss on the feeder supplying the electricity to the 
industrial consumer from 33KV feeder was not solely attributable to the 
petitioner in the face of the fact that three consumers were there and nothing 
was reported that any surprise inspection was conducted upon other two 
consumers and nothing adverse was reported. In paragraph nos. 15 and 16, 
this plea has been taken but in reply thereof, only this much has been stated 
that it need no comments and that provisional assessment order has been 
passed by the competent authority inviting objection and since objection was 
filed to that extent only admission was made by petitioner. 
170→15. In our considered view, this is a very sketchy pleading raised in reply to 
specific pleadings made in the writ petition. Still further, we have carefully 
gone through the objection filed by the petitioner and found that vide 
paragraph nos. 12, 14, 18 sufficient objection was raised which are 
reproduced hereunder:- 
"12. In the meantime on 21.06.2007 the Officers of the PVVNL, namely (i) 
the Executive Engineer, Electricity Test Division, Bijnor, (ii) the 
Executive Engineer, Electricity Distribution Division, Bijnor, (iii) the Sub 
Divisional Officer, and (iv) the Assistant Engineer (Meters) down loaded 
the MRI from the main meter but they did not find anything incriminating 
180→either with the meter or with metering instrument. Those Officers 
properly sealed the main meter and meter cubical vide certificate dated 
21.06.2006. Thus it is clear that up to 21.06.2007, the meter and CT/PT 
of Main Meter were found OK. 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
5

14. That thereafter in the noon of 22.06.2007 the Sub-Divisional 
Magistrate (Chandpur) Bijnor and various other Officials of the PVVNL, 
namely (i) Shri S.N. Yadav Superintending Engineer, Electricity Urban 
190→Distribution Circle, Ghaziabad; (ii) Shri P.S. Gupta, Executive Engineer, 
Electricity Urban Test Division-I, Ghaziabad; (iii) Shri D.C. Chaudhary, 
Executive Engineer, Electricity Test Division, Bijnor; (iv) Shri R.K. 
Sinha, Assistant Engineer, Electricity Urban Test Division-I, Ghaziabad; 
and (v) Shri C.M. Singhal, Junior Engineer (Meter), Electricity Urban 
Test Division-1, Ghaziabad carried out detail checking but they did not 
find anything incriminating either with the main meter or with the 
metering system. When they did not find anything incriminating at all, 
they prepared sealing certificate (Checking /Raid) dated 22.06.2007 and 
mentioned that as per instruction of SE, EUDC, GZB CT/PT chamber of 
200→main meter was opened and CT/PT ratio was found in order. However, 
after completion of checking, the EE, ETD, Bijnor was requested to affix 
seals on the meter. 
18. A cursory glance on check report/ sealing certificate 22.06.2007 
would bear out that neither anything incriminating was found at the 
Objectionist premises nor meter was found tampered. So much so the 
power supply is fed from the said meter electricity charges is being raised 
from the consumption shown in the said meter and, therefore, the 
allegation of unauthorized use of electricity is wholly fallacious and 
misconceived. Had there been any unauthorized use of electricity through 
210→main meter, the department ought to have replaced the said meter by 
installing new meter. Since the main meter is functioning properly the 
presumption regarding correctness of the meter goes in favour of the 
Objectionist." 
16. Further legal plea has been taken to define theft of electricity relying 
upon certain authorities and serious doubts have been raised regarding 
assessment of the inspection report to draw a conclusion of theft from 
conclusion of possibility of theft by the assessing authority. These pleading 
have been raised in paragraph nos. 24, 25, 27, 28, 30, 31, 34 and 35 of the 
objections that are reproduced hereunder:-
220→"24. That the checking team no where alleged that meter was tempered by 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
6

the Objectionist. The check report says that the polycarbonate seals of CT 
& PT chamber found tampered. However, as per the said provision 
neither the CT/PT chamber nor the seals of CT/PT chamber is a part and 
parcel of the meter and, therefore, the Objectionist can not be panelized 
for an assessment of electricity charges for alleged tampering of seals of 
CT chamber.
230→25. That the check report nowhere shows or alleges that the Objectionist 
was drawing electricity illegally or by passing the meter. On the other 
hand it clearly shows that the entire load was connected through meter. 
There is also not even a whisper in the check report that the meter was 
tampered and thus was not in a position to record correct reading. Ex-
facie entire proceeding culminating into provisional assessment notice 
dated 18.07.2007 is patently illegal contrary to law and is in teeth of the 
aforesaid provisions.
27. That in any view of the matter, the provisional assessment notice 
could have been issued, in case, the meter found tampered or electricity is 
240→being drawing through artificial means. However, in the present case, 
neither the meter has been tampered nor the Checking Team had found 
artificial means in the meter and thus no provisional assessment notice 
could have been issued on the basis of check report dated 22.06.2007.
28. That in the matter of Model Terry Towens Limited Versus Gujrat 
Electricity Board, reported in AIR 2003 (Gujrat) 63, the Gujrat High 
Court was pleased to opine that the broken seal does not establish theft of 
electricity. Similar view has been provided in Chamber VIII of Supply 
Code, 2005. Thus provisional notice is wholly illegal and arbitrary.
31. That apart from the above submissions the provisional assessment 
250→notice is barred by time inasmuch as clause 6.8 (vi) of Supply Code, 2005 
provides that within three working days of date of inspection, the 
Assessing Officer shall analyze the case after carefully considering all the 
evidence and if the Assessing Officer suspect that unauthorized use of 
electricity has taken place he will serve provisions assessment bill giving 
15 working days of submission of reply. However, in the present case 
checking was made on 22.06.2007 and the provisional assessment notice 
dated 18.07.2007 has been served to the Objectionist after a lapse of 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
7
260→
almost 26 days and, therefore, the provisional notice is barred by time.
34. That in the provisional assessment notice one of the reason for 
making provisional assessment shown as less consumption of electrical 
energy qua power consumption of the previous year. The Objectionist 
submits that the explanation of Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 
spell out certain conditions for assessment of electricity charges in 
respect to unauthorized use of electricity charges. The said electricity 
thing is no where attracted in present case. It is further stated that making 
of an assessment on the basis of the consumption pattern is absolutely 
270→foreign to the Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003.
35. Similarly, it is alleged that as per the MRI report of 132 KV Sub-
Station and 33 KV Sub-Station the checking team noted that there is line 
losses ranging between 9.17 to 19.75%. The Objectionist submits that the 
Objectionist was/is drawings power supply through mixed feeder. From 
the said feeder M/s Jain Steel & 33/11 KV Sub-Station supplying 
electricity to the Bijnor City are also connected and, therefore, the 
allegation of unauthorized used of electricity on the basis of line losses is 
not permissible under the law. Since the Objectionist is not drawing 
power through an independent feeder, the formula adopted by the 
280→department for making of an assessment for electricity charges on the 
ground of line losses is wholly misconceived and illegal."
17. Upon perusal of the final order of assessment that has been passed on 
23.10.2007, we find that all points and objection have just been referred as 
not acceptable and reliance has been placed upon the report. We further 
notice to our utter surprise that after referring paragraphs of objection to 
reject only, neither the authority applied its mind to the points raised, nor the 
authority bothered even at least to reproduce them so that it could be inferred 
that the some consideration was accorded. We find that the authority has 
concluded that there was an unauthorized use of electricity by way of theft 
290→but we do not find there to be any discussion as to how the report of 
possibility of theft has been converted into a clear case of theft so as to hold 
the petitioner liable for the payment of assessment amount of Rs. 29,52,212/-
. The authority though records that this finding has been reached on the basis 
of analysis but we find that till paragraph no. 33, the authority has referred to 
WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
8

paragraph of the objection of the petitioner to reject the same and in later 
two paragraphs i.e. 34 and 35 only it arrived at a conclusion that since the 
300→seals of the meter system were tempered and loss was reported and 
therefore, it was a case of theft. Paragraph nos. 34, 35 and 36 and the final 
concluding part of the final assessment order dated 23.08.2007 is reproduced 
hereunder:-
"37. Not accepted as it is clearly mentioned in the checking report that 
seal were found tempered and hence action as per rules was to be taken.
Further more analysis of energy flow was carried out which revels that 
there was considerable line losses on this feeder substantiating the fact 
that unauthorized used of electricity has taken place. Also consumption 
was less despites the fact that electricity was supplied for more time then 
310→before. On the basis above mentioned analysis/facts your objection are 
not acceptable. Hence your representation is finalized as follows:-
Your representation is rejected. 
You are kindly requested to deposit the assessment amount 
Rs.29,52,212.00 within 30 days time." 
18. From perusal of the above, therefore, we conclude that there was no 
analysis at all by the final assessing authority to convert the possibility of 
theft into a case of clear theft. We further notice that in appeal several 
grounds were raised questioning the finding so arrived but the appellate 
authority brushed aside those grounds raised by the petitioner and only 
320→refered to the checking report and the summary report to arrive at a 
conclusion that the appeal was devoid of merits and, therefore, deserved 
dismissal and dismissed it. We find that the order dated 08.04.2010 of the 
appellate authority is also an order sans reasons and, therefore, is held 
unsustainable. Still further, since we have already held the final assessment 
order to be bad, the appellate authority affirming the same without 
discussing the grounds and pleadings raised in the appeal also has rendered 
irrelevant. 
19. In view of the above, the writ petition succeeds and is allowed. The 
order passed by the final assessing authority namely, Executive Engineer 
330→WRIC No. 20210 of 2012
9

dated 23.10.2007 and that of the appellate authority dated 11.10.2007 passed 
in statutory Appeal No. 17 of 2007-08 and a consequential order for 
recovery dated 09.04.2012 are all hereby quashed. The matter is remitted to 
the final assessing authority to reconsider the objection filed by the 
petitioner and pass order a fresh recording specific findings to the effect as 
to how and on what basis a case of possibility of theft can be taken as a case 
of actual theft within the meaning of Section 135 of the Electricity Act and 
340→further leading to a case of provisional and final assessment under the U.P. 
Electricity Supply Code, 2005 holding the petitioner liable for payment of 
electricity charges and penalty. An appropriate order shall be passed by the 
assessing authority under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within a 
period of two months from the date of production of certified copy of this 
order.
20. It is made clear that whatever amount has already been deposited shall 
remain deposited with the respondents to be abide by the final order to be 
passed by the assessing authority.

summary.text:
I have a thorough reading of the judgment. Let me also look at related cases for principle tags - especially SCJ-051 (evidentiary threshold for theft), SCJ-060, SCJ-070, SCJ-126 (malice/natural justic...That sounds like a solid case to dig into—especially with the Allahabad High Court’s recent take on how assessments must be reasoned out. The core issue here is that the final assessment order just waved away objections without explaining why the “possibility of theft” (from tampered seals and line losses) actually amounted to 100 % theft or unauthorized use. That’s a classic failure of natural justice, and the court rightly quashed it.

The operative order in para 19 quashes the 23.10.2007 assessment, the 11.10.2007 appellate order (Appeal No. 17 of 2007- 08), and the recovery order of 09.04.2012. The petitioner had framed the writ as challenging the 09.04.2012 appellate order under s. 127, so that’s the docket framing, but the court’s operative paragraph is what actually disposes of the matter.

Key takeaway for 2025-26 practice: any assessment that converts “possibility of theft” into a finding of theft without specific findings on why the checking report’s “no direct theft detected” conclusion is wrong will be set aside.

## Case

**M/S Kamakhya Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. & Others**  
Allahabad High Court (DB) — Ajit Kumar, J. & Swarupama Chaturvedi, J.  
13 February 2026 · Writ-C No. 20210 of 2012

**Disposition:** Petition **allowed**. Final assessment (23.10.2007, Rs. 29,52,212), the s.127 appellate order, and the 09.04.2012 recovery order **quashed**. Remitted for a fresh speaking order within two months. Deposits stay with the licensee pending that order.

## What the Court held

A surprise check that itself records **“no direct theft … possibility of theft”** — from tampered **CT/PT-chamber seals** (main meter not found tampered; no bypass) and **9.17–19.75% line loss on a mixed 33 kV feeder serving three consumers** — cannot, without analysis, be converted into a finding of actual theft under **s.135** or a Code assessment.

The assessing officer marked objections **“not accepted”** without engaging them. The s.127 appeal did the same by pointing only at the checking report. Both orders are **non-speaking**.

Merits of whether theft occurred, the Clause **6.8(vi)** 3-day time-bar, and whether CT/PT seals are part of the “meter” were **not decided**.

Only named authority: **Modern Terry Towels Ltd. v. Gujarat Electricity Board**, AIR 2003 Guj 63 (broken seal ≠ theft) — cited in objections; Court referred, did not independently apply.

## Case

**M/S Ambuja Cements Limited v. U.P. Power Corporation Limited**  
Allahabad High Court — Piyush Agrawal, J.  
26 May 2026 · Arbitration Appl. u/s 11 No. 28 of 2026

**Disposition:** Sole arbitrator appointed (Justice Sudhir Agarwal, former Judge), subject to s.11(8) consent; listed 14.07.2026. Merits left open.

## What it holds (and what it does not)

This is a **Section 11 appointment**, not a Supply Code construction.

UPPCL argued that a penalty for delay in depositing security was imposed under the **2005 Code**, so the consumer must go to the **CGRF/Ombudsman (Clause 7.10)** and the arbitration application is not maintainable.

The Court **did not decide that**. Applying *Mayavati Trading* / *Duro Felguera* / *GOQII Technologies*, s.11(6A) is confined to whether an arbitration agreement exists. One did; an arbitrator was appointed; the Code-forum objection stays open before him.

Indexed under `UP-2005::7.10` only so that objection is findable. It is **not** authority that Clause 7.10 ousts arbitration, or that it does not.

summary.text:
SCJ-277 is thinner than 004/081 - no arrest-safeguard holding, no quashing refusal on merits. Petitioner paid, department will send compounding report, petitioner asked to dispose, court disposed.
The court disposed of the petition under Section 135 CrPC after the department confirmed payment of the assessment and undertook to send a compounding report to the police station. It did not rule that compounding itself bars the FIR or prevents quashing; it simply followed the petitioner’s request once those steps were taken.

## Case

**Anil Kumar Upadhyay v. State of U.P. & 6 Others**  
Allahabad High Court (DB) — Chandra Dhari Singh, J. & Tarun Saxena, J.  
19 August 2026 · Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 7538 of 2026

**Disposition:** Writ **disposed of** on the petitioner’s request. FIR and provisional assessment **not** quashed on the merits.

## What it holds

He had asked to quash a **s.135** FIR (Crime No. 1462/2025, Anti Power Theft, Varanasi) and a **provisional assessment of 01.01.2026**, and to restrain arrest. He also alleged Code/Act violations and sought disciplinary action.

The licensee said the **assessment had been paid** and a **compounding report would go to the police**. He then asked for the petition to be disposed of. The Court agreed. It did **not** decide:
- legality of the FIR or the notice
- whether compounding under s.152 was complete
- the Code-violation / disciplinary prayer

Thin s.135/compounding node (cluster of SCJ-004 / SCJ-081), without the usual arrest-safeguard holding.

proceedings of Sessions Case No. 557 of 2023 (State Vs. Satish Kumar 
Bharti alias Chhotu) arising out of Case Crime No. 667 of 2020 under 
Section 135 of the Indian Electricity Act,  2003, P.S. Anti Power Theft, 
District Chandauli, pending in the Court of Addl. District & Sessions 
Judge, FTC, Chandauli. 
 
3.  Briefly stated facts of the case are that as per the first information 
20→report, during inspection on 26.10.2020, it was found that the applicant 
was found having connected the electricity directly without any valid 
connection. On inquiry, he could not produce any valid document with 
regard to use of the electricity in his premises. Video recording of the 
aforesaid illegal use of electricity was also made and thereafter a first 
information report was lodged on 30.10.2020. Matter was investigated  
and the charge-sheet has been filed against the applicant under Section

40→135 of the Indian Electricity Act on which the cognizance has been taken 
by the Special Judge, Chandauli vide order dated 5.7.2023. 
 
4.   Being aggrieved, the instant application has been filed by the 
applicant seeking quashing of the entire proceedings of the aforesaid 
criminal case lodged against the applicant. 
 
5.  Learned counsel for the applicant has  relied upon second  proviso of 
Section 135 (1) (a) of the  Act and submits that the first information  
report  ought  to have been lodged within 24 hours from the  date  of 
50→inspection when the  electricity theft was found under the  premises of the 
applicant. Since the  first  information  report  was lodged on 30.10.220 
after 4  days, therefore, no cognizance can  be  taken on the said first 
information  report by the  trial  court. Learned counsel for the applicant 
further  submits  that Section  135 (1) provides  five circumstances which 
constitute 5  different offences of theft of electricity and the same has not 
been specified either in the first information report or in the charge-sheet 
or in the order taking cognizance against the applicant. In such view of 
the matter, the  order of cognizance is not sustainable in the  eyes of law 
and he seeks quashing of the entire proceedings against the applicant. 
60→ 
6.  In support of his submission, learned counsel for the applicant has 
relied upon the judgment  of this Court in the case of Varun Kumar  
Yadav Vs.  State of U.P. and others, 2025(7) ADJ 710 and the 
judgment of the  Division Bench of this Court dated 2.12.2023 passed in 
Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 18729 of 2023 (Ashim @ Hassim Vs.  
State  of U.P. and another). 
 
7.  Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the Electricity  Department  
relied upon the judgment  dated 6.2.2013 passed in Criminal Misc. Writ 
70→Petition No. 265 of 2023 (Indresh Patel @ Indreshwar Singh Vs.  
State  of U.P.  and 4  others) and submits  that in the aforesaid judgment, 
the Division  Bench of this Court has held that the aforesaid provision of

electricity,                                                                                                                                      
 
(d) uses electricity through a tampered meter;or  
NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
3

 
(e) uses electricity for the purpose other than for which the usage of 
electricity was authorised, so as to abstract or consume or use electricity 
120→shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 
three years or with fine or with both:
Provided that in a case where the load abstracted, consumed, or used or 
attempted abstraction or attempted consumption or attempted use - 
 
(i) does not exceed 10 kilowatt, the fine imposed on first conviction shall 
not be less than three times the financial gain on account of such theft of 
electricity and in the event of second or subsequent conviction the fine 
imposed shall not be less than six times the financial gain on account of 
such theft of electricity; 
130→ 
(ii) exceeds 10 kilowatt, the fine imposed on first conviction shall not be 
less than three times the financial gain on account of such theft of 
electricity and in the event of second or subsequent conviction, the 
sentence shall be imprisonment for a term not less than six months, but 
which may extend to five years and with fine not less than six times the 
financial gain on account of such theft of electricity: 
Provided further that in the event of second and subsequent conviction of 
a person where the load abstracted, consumed, or used or attempted 
abstraction or attempted consumption or attempted use exceeds 10 
140→kilowatt, such person shall also be debarred from getting any supply of 
electricity for a period which shall not be less than three months but may 
extend to two years and shall also be debarred from getting supply of 
electricity for that period from any other source or generating station: 
Provided also that if it is proved that any artificial means or means not 
authorized by the Board or licensee or supplier, as the case may be, exist 
for the abstraction, consumption or use of electricity by the consumer, it 
shall be presumed, until the contrary is proved, that any abstraction, 
consumption or use of electricity has been dishonestly caused by such 
consumer. 
150→ 
(1-A) Without prejudice to the provisions of this Act, the licensee or 
supplier, as the case may be, may, upon detection of such theft of 
NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
4

electricity, immediately disconnect the supply of electricity: 
Provided that only such officer of the licensee or supplier, as authorized 
for the purpose by the Appropriate Commission or any other officer of the 
licensee or supplier, as the case may be, of the rank higher than the rank 
160→so authorised shall disconnect the supply line of electricity: Provided 
further that such officer of the licensee or supplier, as the case may be, 
shall lodge a complaint in writing relating to the commission of such 
offence in police station having jurisdiction within twenty four hours from 
the time of such disconnection: Provided also that the licensee or 
supplier, as the case may be, on deposit or payment of the assessed 
amount or electricity charges in accordance with the provisions of this 
Act, shall, without prejudice to the obligation to lodge the complaint as 
referred to in the second proviso to this clause, restore the supply line of 
electricity within forty-eight hours of such deposit or payment.] 
170→ 
(2) [Any officer of the licensee or supplier as the case may be,] 
authorized in this behalf by the State Government may – (a) enter, 
inspect, break open and search any place or premises in which he has 
reason to believe that electricity [has been or is being,] used 
unauthorisedly; 
(b) search, seize and remove all such devices, instruments, wires and any 
other facilitator or article which has been, or is being, used for 
unauthorized use of electricity; 
(c) examine or seize any books of account or documents which in his 
180→opinion shall be useful for or relevant to, any proceedings in respect of 
the offence under sub-section (1) and allow the person from whose 
custody such books of account or documents are seized to make copies 
thereof or take extracts therefrom in his presence. 
 
(3) The occupant of the place of search or any person on his behalf shall 
remain present during the search and a list of all things seized in the 
course of such search shall be prepared and delivered to such occupant 
or person who shall sign the list: Provided that no inspection, search and 
seizure of any domestic places or domestic premises shall be carried out 
190→between sunset and sunrise except in the presence of an adult male 
member occupying such premises.
NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
5

(4) The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, relating to 
search and seizure shall apply, as far as may be, to searches and seizure 
under this Act."
 
10. Section 135 of the Electricity Act deals with the theft of electricity, 
200→and sub-section (1) provides various categories of offenses which come 
within the purview of theft of electricity. However, the punishment 
provided for all the categories mentioned in sub-section (1) of Section 
135 is the same, i.e. imprisonment of a term which may extend to 3 years 
or with fine or with both.  In the considered opinion of this court narration
of the offence made in the FIR categorically mentions that the offense is 
under Section 135 (1 ) as there was no authorized electricity connection in
the premises of the applicant herein. However, he was found using the 
electricity by laying the cable illegally. Videography of the same was also
made. He was unable to show any document  for such use of electricity 
210→nor he has produced any document before this court, which authorized 
him to use the electricity.  The different categories provided under sub-
section (1) of Section 135 can be seen as the definition of theft of 
electricity. Therefore, this court do not find any illegality in non-
mentioning of the specific category as mentioned in sub-section (1) of 
Section 135 in the FIR or in the charge sheet and the cognizance order, 
because the offence is mentioned under section 135, though the different 
categories are there, which is nothing but only the definition, which 
includes the offense of theft of electricity. Reliance placed by learned 
counsel for the applicant in the judgment of Ashim @ Hassim (supra) 
220→cannot be applied in the instant case, as the same relates to the Gangster 
Act and entirely different connotation have been made to the different 
offenses under the Gangster Act. In Indresh Patel (supra), the Division 
Bench of this Court has taken a view that the period of 24 hours as 
provided in second proviso to Section 135 (1-A) of the Electricity Act is 
directory and no consequences otherwise specified for the breach of its 
conditions. However, the Coordinate Bench in Varun Kumar Yadav 
(supra) has taken a different view and has applied the principle that once 
a particular thing is directed to be done in a particular manner, anything 
done otherwise will be void and illegal, as has been held by the Apex 
230→NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
6

Court in Dr. Arun Kumar v. Nagar Nigam, Bareilly 2017 (2) ADJ 638. 
Against the judgment of Varun Kumar Yadav (supra),  SLP has been 
filed and the same is still pending before the Apex Court.
 
11. Learned counsel for the applicant herein has further relied upon the 
Section 57 of the Electricity Act which provides for the standard of 
performance by licensee, and sub-section (2) of Section 57 provides that 
240→if the licensee fails to meet the standards specified under sub-section 
(1),without prejudice to any penalty which may be imposed or 
prosecution be initiated, it shall be liable to pay such compensation to the 
person affected as may be determined by the appropriate commission. 
Learned counsel for the applicant further relied upon clause 8.2 of the UP 
Electricity Supply Code 2005, which also reaffirms that the complaint 
before the police ought to have been lodged within 24 hours and the case 
in this regard to be filed before the special court within 30 days and 
failure to lodge the case within 30 days before the special court would 
attract the obligations under Section 57 of the Electricity Act. Thus, the 
250→consequences for non-compliance of provisions of Section 135 (1-A) i.e. 
to lodge the FIR within 24 hours, is categorically provided in the 
Electricity Code as well as Section 57 of the Electricity Act. Therefore, 
the observations made by the Division Bench of this Court in Indresh 
Patel (supra) that no consequences are provided are the per incuriam 
observations, which have been observed without looking into the 
provisions of Section 57 and clause 8.2 of the Electricity Supply Code 
2005. Therefore, the judgment of Indresh Patel (supra) in the considered
opinion of this court, being per incuriam, is not a binding precedent. 
Having held so, since the clear consequences are provided in the 
260→Electricity Act as well as the Electricity Supply Code, and the Act 
provides that the criminal proceedings ought to have been lodged within 
24 hours of such disconnection made by the licensee.  
 
12. It is admitted case that the FIR was lodged after 4 days much beyond 
the period of 24 hours.  In such view of the matter, relying upon the 
judgment of Varun Kumar Yadav (supra), the instant application is 
allowed and the entire proceeding of Sessions Case No. 557 of 2023 
NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
7
270→
(State Vs. Satish Kumar Bharti alias Chhotu) arising out of Case Crime 
No. 667 of 2020 under Section 135 of the Indian Electricity Act,  2003, 
P.S. Anti Power Theft, District Chandauli, pending in the Court of Addl. 
District & Sessions Judge, FTC, Chandauli are hereby quashed against 
the applicant herein. The respondent no. 2 is further directed to initiate 
appropriate proceedings against respondent no. 3, who has failed to lodge 
the FIR within the stipulated period, as mandated under Section 135 (1) 
(a) of the Act, 2003.
June 29, 2026
280→n.u./o.k.
NA528 No. 36991 of 2025
8
(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.)
Digitally signed by :- 
NASEEM UDDIN 
High Court of Judicature at Allahabad

30→      "topic": "For assessment of theft of electricity under s.135, Clauses 8.1/8.2 of the Supply Code (not Clause 6.8) govern; Clause 8.1(b)(iii) requires 15 working days' show-cause notice and Clause 8.1(b)(iv) mandates assessment at 1.5 times (not 3 times) the applicable tariff if theft is established after hearing",
      "type": "supply_code",
      "question": "Which Supply Code procedure — Clause 6.8 (general unauthorised use) or Clauses 8.1/8.2 (theft-specific) — governs assessment where theft of electricity under s.135 is alleged, and did the assessing officer follow the correct procedure and tariff multiplier?",
      "holding": "Following Mohit Paper Mills (applying the specific-prevails-over-general canon), Clauses 8.1/8.2 govern theft-based assessment, not Clause 6.8. On the facts, the assessing officer's provisional-assessment notice (25.5.2007) gave only one week (not the mandated 15 working days), lacked specificity as to which s.135(1) clause was invoked, and calculated the provisional assessment at thrice (not 1.5 times) the applicable tariff — all procedural lapses reflecting negligence or lack of legal clarity by the (technically-trained, non-legal) assessing officer, for which the licensee bears responsibility to provide adequate training. However, since the petitioner's only reply (31.5.2007) addressed occupancy, not the theft allegation or quantum, and the assessing officer's own subsequent (albeit procedurally chaotic) self-correction reduced the assessment to the correct 1.5x multiplier (Rs. 21,17,016, down from Rs. 42,78,355), and given the clearly-established theft on the inspection record (a 160 KVA transformer improperly connected via temporary L.T. line to run an ice factory with no sanctioned connection), the Court declined to interfere with the corrected final assessment despite the demonstrated procedural laxity — noting the Court, exercising equity under Article 226, would not assist a demonstrably blameworthy party on technicalities causing loss to public revenue.",
      "limiting_facts": "A raid (14.5.2007) at premises owned by the petitioner (running 'Kanchi Ice Factory') detected a direct L.T. connection bypassing any sanctioned meter, drawing power from a 160 KVA transformer; provisional assessment (Rs. 42,78,355, at 3x tariff) was issued 25.5.2007; the petitioner's reply addressed only alleged non-occupancy; the assessing officer's conduct included an inexplicably backdated/ante-dated 'final assessment' order (dated 23.5.2007, i.e. before the provisional assessment and the petitioner's reply) which the Court found deeply troubling but not, on the facts, fatal to the ultimately-corrected assessment.",

Processed as **SCJ-278** (`NA528(A)_36991_2025.pdf`). This one is a real doctrinal node, not a thin listing.

## Case

**Satish Kumar Bharti alias Chhotu v. State of U.P. & 2 Others**  
Allahabad High Court — Anish Kumar Gupta, J.  
29 June 2026 · Application u/s 528 BNSS No. 36991 of 2025

**Disposition:** Application **allowed**. Sessions Case No. 557 of 2023 (s.135 theft, Chandauli) **quashed**. Licensee directed to proceed against the officer who lodged the FIR late.

## What it holds

**1. 24-hour FIR is mandatory.**  
s.135(1-A) second proviso + **Clause 8.2** of the 2005 Code (police complaint in 24 hours; Special Court in 30 days) + **s.57** compensation for missed standards. An FIR four days after the 26.10.2020 inspection is void.

**2. *Indresh Patel* (DB) is per incuriam.**  
That Bench called the 24-hour rule directory because it saw no consequences. This Court: Clause 8.2 and s.57 *are* the consequences. Follows coordinate Bench in ***Varun Kumar Yadav*** 2025 (7) ADJ 710 even though SLP (Crl.) Diary No. 74474 of 2025 is pending.

**3. s.135(1)(a)–(e) are the definition of theft**, not five offences that must be named. Same punishment. Narration of a direct illegal cable with no authorised connection is enough. *Ashim @ Hassim* (Gangster Act) distinguished.

**Recorded, not cleaned up:** the 1-A clock runs from *disconnection*, not inspection; the Court used the inspection-to-FIR gap. The last direction cites “s.135(1)(a)” for the 24-hour rule (that is the tapping offence; the clock is 1-A). Tension with the Division Bench is left on the table.

LUCKNOW
APPLICATION U/S 528 BNSS No. - 2047 of 2026
Court No. - 16 
HON'BLE SHREE PRAKASH SINGH, J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Mr. Amit Kumar Dwivedi, learned 
counsel for the Electricity Department, and learned AGA for the State. 
The instant application under Section 528 BNSS has been filed with the 
following prayers:-
10→"I. ISSUE AN ORDER OR DIRECTION quashing the Charge Sheet No. 544/2025 
dated 10.09.2025, as well as the entire proceedings of Sessions Case/2082 of 2025 
(State vs. Shah Faisal), arising out of F.I.R. No.1466/2022, registered under Section 
135 of the Electricity Act, 2003, at Police Station Anti-Power Theft (APT), District 
Sitapur, currently pending before the learned Special Judge (Electricity Act), Sitapur;
II. ISSUE AN ORDER OR DIRECTION setting aside the Inspection Report dated 
02.11.2022 and the consequential Impugned Revenue Assessment of ₹5,96,266/-, 
being void initio and legally unsustainable due to gross non-compliance with 
the mandatory procedural requirements of Para 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity 
Supply Code, 2005, specifically regarding the lack of mandatory videography 
20→and the absence of independent public witnesses;
III. ISSUE AN ORDER OR DIRECTION to the Opposite Party No. 1 and 2 to 
constitute an independent inquiry/investigation into the departmental entrapment and 
the fraudulent role of the local departmental staff in the unauthorized installation of a 
government-grade transformer and departmental corruption of Opposite Parties No. 
Versus
Counsel for Applicant(s)
:
Pawan Verma, Arvind Kumar Maurya, 
Kanchan
30→Counsel for Opposite Party(s) :
G.A.
Shah Faisal
.....Applicant(s)
State Of Uttar Pradesh Through Additional Chief 
Secretary, Home And 4 Others
.....Opposite 
Party(s)

5, who extorted ₹2,05,000 from the Petitioner." 
40→Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and 
he has been falsely implicated in the present case with false and frivolous 
allegations. The applicant has not committed alleged offence.
On the other hand, learned AGA has submitted that prima facie, the offence 
is made out against the applicant. It is further submitted that these are 
disputed questions of fact, which can be adjudicated only after adducing the 
evidence. He further controverts the submissions of learned counsel for the 
applicant on the ground that this is not a stage where minute and meticulous 
exercise with regard to the appreciation of evidence may be done and 
truthfulness of the allegations could only be tested in a criminal trial and, 
50→therefore, the application is misconceived and liable to be dismissed.  
At this stage, learned counsel for the applicant submits that he does not want 
to press the application and seeks liberty to file bail application before the 
learned trial court which may be decided in view of law laid by Hon'ble 
Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau 
of Investigation and another, (2022) 10 SCC 51.  
Learned A.G.A. has no objection to the prayer made by learned counsel for 
the applicant.
On due consideration to the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, it 
is provided that in case, the applicant appears before the trial court within 
60→two weeks from today and files bail application, the same shall be decided 
expeditiously in view of law laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil 
versus Central Bureau of Investigation and another (supra).
The application is disposed off accordingly.

## Case

**Shah Faisal v. State of Uttar Pradesh & 4 Others**  
Allahabad High Court (Lucknow) — Shree Prakash Singh, J.  
6 July 2026 · Application u/s 528 BNSS No. 2047 of 2026

**Disposition:** Application **disposed of as not pressed**. Two weeks to appear and file bail; trial court to decide it expeditiously per *Satender Kumar Antil* (2022) 10 SCC 51.

## What it holds (and does not)

He had asked to quash a **s.135** charge-sheet (FIR 1466/2022, Anti-Power Theft, Sitapur) and to set aside the 02.11.2022 inspection and a **Rs. 5,96,266** assessment for want of **Clause 8.1** videography and independent public witnesses. He also alleged departmental entrapment.

The State said a prima facie case was made out and the facts were for trial. Counsel then **did not press**. The Court did **not** construe Clause 8.1, did **not** touch the assessment, and did **not** quash the charge-sheet.

Indexed under `UP-2005::8.1` only because that was the Code ground pleaded.

1→HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 10722 of 2026
Court No. - 1 
HON'BLE AJIT KUMAR, J.
HON'BLE INDRAJEET SHUKLA, J.
1. Heard Mr. Istiyaq Ali, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and 
Mr. Ram Chandra, learned Advocate holding brief of Mr. Pranjal 
Mehrotra, learned Counsel for the Electricity Department.
2. By means of this writ petition filed under Article 226 of the 
10→Constitution of India, petitioner has prayed for quashing of the recovery 
citation dated 07.10.2025 issued by respondent no.6.
3. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that no provisional 
assessment notice was ever issued to the petitioner to enable him to file 
objection under Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
4. Mr. Ram Chanra, learned Advocate has placed instructions, which are 
taken on record, copy of which is also supplied to learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
5. From the instructions it transpires that the final assessment order has 
come to be passed on 24.03.2026. It further transpires that this order was 
20→based upon provisional assessment notice issued on 27.03.2025 and the 
recital contained in the order is to the effect that petitioner did not submit 
reply despite given time to file objections, however,  from the perusal of 
records we do not find there to be any receipt appended along with 
instructions so as to draw inference that the petitioner was duly served 
with the provisional assessment notice.
Versus
Counsel for Petitioner(s)
:
Ali Hasan, Istiyaq Ali
30→Counsel for Respondent(s)
:
C.S.C., Pranjal Mehrotra
Shahvez Abdullah
.....Petitioner(s)
State Of U.P. And 6 Others
.....Respondent(s)

6. In the circumstances, therefore, while taking judicial notice of the order 
dated 24.03.2026, which is final assessment order, we dispose of this 
40→petition with a direction to the petitioner to treat the final assessment 
order as provisional assessment and file his objection within four weeks 
from today. We further provide that in the event petitioner files his 
objection within four weeks from today, no coercive action shall be taken 
against him pursuant to recovery notice. Further, in the event, the 
petitioner files an objection, he shall be afforded opportunity of hearing 
and final assessment order shall be passed within a further period of one 
month. In the circumstances, the recovery citation dated 24.03.2026 is put 
in abeyance to abide by final outcome/decision taken by the authorities 
concerned.
50→April 23, 2026
S.P.
WRIC No. 10722 of 2026
2
(Indrajeet Shukla,J.)   (Ajit Kumar,J.)
Digitally signed by :- 
SANJAY PURI 
High Court of Judicature at Allahabad

Processed as **SCJ-280** (`WRIC(A)_10722_2026.pdf`).

## Case

**Shahvez Abdullah v. State of U.P. & 6 Others**  
Allahabad High Court (DB) — Ajit Kumar, J. & Indrajeet Shukla, J.  
23 April 2026 · Writ-C No. 10722 of 2026

**Disposition:** Petition **disposed of**. The 24.03.2026 “final” assessment is to be **treated as provisional**. Objections in four weeks; hearing; fresh final order in one further month. Recovery **in abeyance** if he files in time.

## What it holds

He said no provisional assessment notice was ever served, so he could not object under the Supply Code. The licensee’s instructions recited a provisional notice of 27.03.2025 and a final order of 24.03.2026 (no reply). **No receipt of service** was on the record.

Without proof of service, a “final” assessment cannot support recovery. Same cluster as SCJ-014 / 022 / 028 / 117 (`opportunity-before-final-assessment`).

The Court did not number 6.8 vs 8.1 (keyed to 8.1 with a flag). Quantum not decided. Recovery citation is dated 07.10.2025 in para 2 and 24.03.2026 in the operative paragraph — recorded as stated.

1→HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 10937 of 2026
Court No. - 29 
HON'BLE ARINDAM SINHA, J.
HON'BLE SATYA VEER SINGH, J.
1. With reference to earlier order dated 2nd April, 2026, Mr. Chetan 
Chatterjee, learned advocate appearing for respondent nos. 3 to 8 (the supply 
company) files affidavit dated 5th April, 2026 with copy served to Mr. 
Santosh Kumar Singh, learned advocate appearing for petitioner.
10→2. Mr. Chatterjee relies on clauses 4.5 (d) and 4.6 (e)(ii) and (iii) in Uttar 
Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He submits, petitioner had initially 
opted to establish the connection requiring his client to only charge 
supervision costs. Subsequently, he wanted the supply to be given by his 
client (the supply company). Hence, there was revised estimate. It has been 
challenged in the writ petition. The challenge is without merit. The writ 
petition be dismissed.
3. Clauses (a) to (d) from clause 4.5 are reproduced below.
"4.5 Inspection by Licensee: 
The applicant along with the licensed contractor or his representative 
20→shall be present during the inspection. During the inspection, the 
Licensee shall:
(a) Satisfy themselves regarding the work completion certificate and the 
test report submitted by the applicant.
(b) In consultation with the applicant, fix the point of supply and the place 
where meter and the MCB etc. shall be fixed.
(c) Estimate the distance between the point of supply and the nearest 
Distribution mains from where supply could be given.
Versus
Counsel for Petitioner(s)
30→:
Santosh Kumar Singh
Counsel for Respondent(s)
:
C.S.C., Chetan Chatterjee
Abhimanyu Singh
.....Petitioner(s)
State Of Up And 7 Others
.....Respondent(s)

40→(d) Determine if the supply line shall go over any property belonging to a 
third party. In such a case the applicant shall obtain no objection from 
the third party, in absence of which, the licensee may adopt a different 
route for which the applicant shall bear the cost differential.
....................." 
Clause 4.6 (e) (ii) and (iii) is also reproduced below.
"4.6 Estimate
........................
(e) (i) ..............
(ii) If the work is to be done by the developer/applicant/ development 
50→authority, the Licensee shall charge supervision charges (on the 
estimated labour cost, cost of material, material handling and 
storage/inventory, but excluding the system loading charges and the 
establishment costs), as a percentage of the normative estimates, specified 
in cost data book, which shall be deposited with the licensee before work 
begins.
For LT Loads upto 50 kW, if the supply released on HT on the request of 
consumers (in such cases, metering will be done on LT and billing as per 
LT tariff)-15%.
For Loads exceeding 50 KW (56 KVA) upto 3600 KW (4000 KVA)-15%.
60→For Loads exceeding 3600 KW upto 9000 KW (10,000 KVA)-8%
For Loads exceeding 9000 KW (10,000 KVA)-5%.
Notwithstanding the amended provision coming into effect from the date 
of notification, the supervision charge on cost of material charged earlier 
in the estimates before this amendment shall not be refunded back.
(iii) The Licensee shall commence the work after the applicant has 
deposited the full amount of the estimates.
........................."
Our understanding of above relied upon provisions is that the direct 
transmission from distribution main to point of supply is at cost of the 
70→licencee (the supply company). In event of objection requiring alternate 
route, the differential in cost is to be borne by applicant.
4. Prayer (a) in the petition is reproduced below.
"a) Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of mandamus directing 
the electricity department to immediate give electricity connection to the 
petitioner tube well in pursuance of the estimate amount paid by the 
petitioner a sum of Rs. 1,19,368 on 18.08.2025 with immediate effect 
WRIC No. 10937 of 2026
2

80→without any delay."
Petitioner is facing objection from his neighbours on asserting, his property is 
landlocked. The supply company is directed to give particulars on fresh estimate, for 
petitioner to pay on the differential cost. Particulars are to be furnished to petitioner to 
show cost involved for setting up direct transmission between the distribution main 
and point of supply as well as the longer route of transmission, necessitated by the 
objection(s), for demanding the estimate of cost from petitioner. In event it is less than 
amount already deposited by petitioner, the difference to be adjusted from future 
consumption bills. Otherwise, the excess will be informed to petitioner, for him to pay 
and obtain the supply.
90→5. Petitioner will communicate certified copy of this order to respondent no. 6. Within 
two weeks of the communication, the exercise is to be completed and petitioner given 
the supply. This time line will stand automatically extended in case petitioner does not 
fulfill requirement of paying the excess, if demonstrated to be payable.
6. The writ petition is disposed of. 
April 9, 2026
sailesh
WRIC No. 10937 of 2026
3

summary.text:
This is a real Supply Code construction case on Clauses 4.5(d) and 4.6(e).
Under the court's reading of Clauses 4.5(d) and 4.6, the licensee must bear the base cost of running the direct supply line from the distribution main to the point of supply.

1→HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 11370 of 2026
Court No. - 29 
HON'BLE ARINDAM SINHA, J.
HON'BLE SATYA VEER SINGH, J.
1. The writ petition was moved on 25th March, 2026. Mr. Arun Mishra, 
learned advocate appearing for petitioner had submitted, prayer of his 
client was for issuance of mandamus to command respondent no.2 (the 
Executive Engineer) to generate one bill from inception of the connection, 
10→on the basis of final reading of 4468KWH units without adding fixed 
charge after line temporarily disconnected under clause 4.37(a) in Uttar 
Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and without surcharge. Drawing 
attention to clause 4.37(a) he had submitted, the provision mandates the 
licensee to bill a consumer on minimum charges after a connection is 
temporarily disconnected. The licensee is to thereafter move for 
permanent disconnection.
2. Paragraphs-2 and 3 from order dated 25th March, 2026 are reproduced 
below.
"2. Mr. Rakesh Kumar Mishra, learned advocate holding the brief 
20→appears on behalf of respondents (the supply company). He draws 
attention to order dated 12th December, 2025 made by co-ordinate Bench 
in petitioner's own case (Writ C no.- 43924 of 2025). Pursuant to said 
order, petitioner made representation and the bill dated 20th February, 
2026 was generated. He points out from the bill, there is deduction. 
Petitioner's grievance was taken care of.
3. Mr. Arun Mishra in reply demonstrates from the bill, there is amount of 
Versus
Counsel for Petitioner(s)
:
30→Arun Mishra, Vijay Pratap Singh, 
Vishnu Pratap Pandey
Counsel for Respondent(s)
:
Narendra Kumar Tiwari
Parvati Devi
.....Petitioner(s)
Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam And Another
.....Respondent(s)

40→Rs. 2,24,241.30/- as late payment surcharge. Referring to clause 6.5(b)(i) 
he submits, clear provision is for no payment on late payment surcharge 
when a bill is revised upon consumer's complaint found to be correct."
3. The writ petition was then called and heard on 1st April, 2026. On that 
day there was query made by Court. Record of the query and answer 
given by Mr. Mishra, as appearing from order order dated 1st April, 2026, 
are reproduced below.
"On query, Mr. Arun Mishra points out, there was disconnection on 
disconnection memo issued on 21st March, 2025 indicating demand of 
Rs.4,23,419/-. His client complained. Revised bill dated 20th February, 
50→2026 was issued on reduced demand of Rs.3,68,494/-. This sum includes 
late payment surcharge of Rs.2,24,241.30/-. He reiterates his prayer for 
interference."
It further appears from said order dated 1st April, 2026 that the 
controversy had boiled down to demand of surcharge at Rs. 2,24,241.30/-. 
There was direction for petitioner to deposit the difference between the 
disputed billed amount less the surcharge and corresponding direction 
upon the supply company to disclose particulars in support of the demand 
for surcharge, as levied on earlier arrears. In this context paragraph-4 
from said order dated 1st April, 2026 is reproduced below.
60→"4. Petitioner to deposit Rs.1,44,253/- (bill amount less the surcharge) on 
or prior to adjourned date. Omission will lead to dismissal of the writ 
petition. The supply company will produce the particulars in support of 
said disconnection memo dated 21st March, 2025. It be disclosed on 
affidavit, to be accepted on adjourned date upon advance copy served."
4. Today, Mr. N.K. Tiwari, learned advocate appearing for respondents 
(the supply company) files affidavit dated 7th April, 2026 with copy 
served to Mr. Mishra. He submits, it is in compliance with direction for 
disclosing the particulars. Mr. Mishra submits, his client cannot be 
required to make the deposit. He wants to demonstrate from the affidavit 
70→filed, 'Ok' bill dated 21st May, 2019 has not been produced/disclosed. He 
refers to sub-clause (a) under clause 4.37. The sub-clause is reproduced 
below.
WRIC No. 11370 of 2026
2

"4.37 (a) The Licensee shall, after a connection is temporarily 
disconnected, bill a consumer on minimum charges, and also issue a 
notice, as per format given in Annexure 4.9, to the consumer, to remove 
the cause of disconnection failing which, the supply shall be 
80→disconnected permanently after six months. Such connections shall be 
treated as dormant connections (awaiting final account), and the billing 
shall be stopped after carrying out inspections and duly informing the 
consumer, and final account of the consumer shall be prepared."
(emphasis supplied)  
Clause 4.38 is also reproduced below.  
"4.38 Permanent Disconnection.
(i) The supply shall be disconnected permanently in following cases:
(a) With the termination of the agreement.
(b) If the cause for which the supply was temporarily disconnected is 
90→not removed within six months period.
(c) On request of consumer as described under section 4.14(g)"
(emphasis supplied)
He submits, there is mandate for permanent disconnection. That is his 
client's prayer.
5. Prayers made in the petition are reproduced below.
"i) Issue a writ of mandamus commanding respondent no. 2 to generate 
one bill from inception of connection on the basis of final reading of 4468 
KWH unit, No fixed charge after line temporarily disconnected U/clause 
4.38 of U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and without surcharge.
100→ii) Issue writ of certiorari quashing bill dated 20.02.2026 issued by 
respondent no. 2."
Petitioner has sought quashing of bill dated 20th February, 2026. Court, 
WRIC No. 11370 of 2026
3

upon hearing submissions made on behalf of petitioner had tried to 
determine controversy between the parties, to find dispute on the 
surcharge. On behalf of petitioner Mr. Mishra submits, his client is not 
required to deposit the difference because there must be permanent 
110→disconnection.
6. Petitioner was expected to pay the difference, which she has refused to 
deposit on direction made obviously as a pre-condition to look into her 
grievance in respect of allegedly wrongful imposition of the surcharge 
Her contention in disputing the difference will draw the writ Court into a 
dispute in respect of  the billed amount. We refuse to be so drawn. 
Furthermore, the supply company is empowered by clauses 4.37 and 4.38 
to permanently disconnect a line temporarily disconnected, the cause for 
which has not been removed. Whether or not petitioner can compel the 
supply company to do something that it is empowered to do is not a 
120→question for consideration in the writ petition, where the bill itself is 
disputed.
7. For reasons aforesaid we will not interfere. The writ petition is 
dismissed. 
April 8, 2026
Shiraz
WRIC No. 11370 of 2026
4
 
(Arindam Sinha,J.)

SHIRAZ ALI

## Case

**Parvati Devi v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another**  
Allahabad High Court (DB) — Arindam Sinha, J. & Satya Veer Singh, J.  
8 April 2026 · Writ-C No. 11370 of 2026

**Disposition:** Writ **dismissed**.

## What it holds

After a prior writ she got a revised bill (20.02.2026) that still carried **Rs. 2,24,241.30 LPS**. She wanted a recast bill from inception (4468 kWh), no fixed charges after temporary disconnection, no surcharge — citing **Clauses 4.37(a), 4.38 and 6.5(b)(i)**.

The Court had required deposit of **Rs. 1,44,253** (bill minus surcharge) before looking at LPS. She refused, saying 4.37/4.38 *mandate* permanent disconnection.

**Holdings:**
- The writ court will **not** try a billed-amount / surcharge dispute if the undisputed part is not deposited.
- Clauses **4.37 and 4.38 empower the licensee** to permanently disconnect after six months of unremedied TD. Whether the *consumer* can *compel* that is **not** a question in a bill-dispute writ.

**Clause 6.5(b)(i)** (no LPS on a correctly revised bill) was **not decided**.

1→HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
WRIT - C No. - 12255 of 2026
Court No. - 29 
HON'BLE ARINDAM SINHA, J.
HON'BLE SATYA VEER SINGH, J.
1. Mr. Praval Tripathi, learned advocate appears on behalf of private 
respondent nos. 9 to 11 and files affidavit of date on copy served to Mr. 
Kumar Vinay Singh, learned advocate appearing for petitioner. He 
submits, there is dispute in respect of the land, over which petitioner 
10→wants the transmission line to be drawn, for purpose of obtaining electric 
connection. He relies on clause 4.5 (d) in Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply 
Code, 2005. The provision is reproduced below. 
"4.5 Inspection by Licensee
.....(d) Determine if the supply line shall go over any property belonging 
to a third party. In such a case the applicant shall obtain no objection 
from the third party, in absence of which, the licensee may adopt a 
different route for which the applicant shall bear the cost differential." 
(emphasis supplied) 
Mr. Sharad Chandra Upadhyay, learned advocate, Standing Counsel 
20→appears on behalf of State and Mr. Nitesh Patel, learned advocate holding 
the brief, for respondent nos. 2, 6 and 7 (the supply company). 
2. Private respondents contend that where there is objection by a third 
party, connection must be obtained from different route for which 
applicant shall bear the cost differential. Mr. Singh submits, private 
respondents are encroachers. The land belongs to the Gram Sabha. 
Versus
Counsel for Petitioner(s)
:
Kumar Abhay Singh, Kumar Vinay 
30→Singh
Counsel for Respondent(s)
:
C.S.C., Udit Chandra
Kumar Ajay Singh
.....Petitioner(s)
The State Of U.P. And 10 Others
.....Respondent(s)

Litigation in respect of purported dispute is carrying on for past 28 years. 
40→There be direction because his client will not be able to run the pump on 
alternative domestic supply. 
3. On query Mr. Tripathi submits, his client preferred appeal. The title 
dispute has been remanded to respondent no.5 (Tehsildar). The authority 
is in seisen of the controversy regarding ownership of the land. In the 
circumstances, the supply company must approach said respondent for 
obtaining 'no objection'. The supply company is to accordingly apply to 
respondent no.5 and for the purpose, may enclose website copy of this 
order. The application be dealt with in the time of adjournment granted. 
4. Respondent no.5 will file affidavit enclosing the decision taken. It will 
50→be accepted on adjourned date, upon advance copy served. For the 
purpose of taking decision, said respondent may notice private 
respondents and the Gram Sabha. The supply company also to work out 
alternative route and differential in cost and provide the same by way of 
affidavit, also to be accepted on adjourned date, upon advance copy 
served. 
5. List on 6th July, 2026 as fresh.  
May 26, 2026
Mohini
